mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues to fall while TRANSIT stays near its current depressed level, weekday foot traffic weakens and retail-and-recreation mobility should drift lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining below -40 and TRANSIT staying below -45 for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed shift toward staying home, visible as rising RESIDENTIAL mobility and weaker outside activity, substitutes away from discretionary shopping trips and pushes RETAIL_REC down within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises by at least 1 point week-on-week while WORKPLACES falls by at least 2 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after a week in which RESIDENTIAL rises and WORKPLACES falls by the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT drops sharply while GROCERY_PHARM also weakens, it indicates tighter movement constraints rather than pure substitution, and discretionary retail mobility should fall over the following month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -52 and GROCERY_PHARM falls below -20 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 28 days after the joint threshold is crossed for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in PARKS mobility during weekends signals more outdoor leisure substitution, and that leisure demand spills into nearby retail activity, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean even though PARKS improves by at least 3 points for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds from the current trough while TRANSIT does not deteriorate further, commuting-linked errands recover and RETAIL_REC turns higher over a one-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 2 points from one week to the next and TRANSIT stays above -53
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week after WORKPLACES posts a rebound and TRANSIT remains above the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous fall in GROCERY_PHARM and rise in RESIDENTIAL means households are consolidating trips at home, which reduces discretionary visits to retail venues over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -22 while RESIDENTIAL exceeds 15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days of the joint grocery weakness and residential strength condition.

mechanism_narrative: In a restrictions-tightening regime, a renewed decline in TRANSIT is an early leading indicator of lower discretionary mobility, so RETAIL_REC should weaken over four weeks after the transit drop.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by 2 or more points week-on-week from a level already below -50
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the prior 28 days after a qualifying TRANSIT decline.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both strengthen at the same time, people substitute toward local outdoor and home activity instead of shopping trips, so retail-and-recreation mobility falls over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over 28 days following a period in which PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both rise for at least two consecutive weeks.
